utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Our apologies for the belated start. But unfortunately a legal officer fell ill, and we are grateful that we have an immediate replacement, if I may say so. Anything to be discussed before the start? This is not the case. May I ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, please. And then in the meantime we can call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Budimir. Sorry for the delay. Due to the fact that a legal officer fell ill, we had to start a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, as a matter of principle, did you have any contacts with one of the parties during the testimony, we'll say in the evening, in the afternoon until now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any contacts with either party except with an acquaintance of mine who is going to testify after me. We are in the same hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I wouldn't be surprised that this would be Mr. Travar. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask Mr. Koumjian to continue your line of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, in the article that we looked at yesterday afternoon regarding Mr. Medunjanin, it indicated that he was captured with his personal Winchester rifle. Are you familiar with this generally with this type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be correct from your knowledge of military hardware that this is not a weapon issued in the JNA at that time and was not a military-issue weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am no expert for military weapons. I know very little about weapons as a matter of fact. But as far as I know, the available weaponry, the range of weaponry available to the JNA did not include this. However, I never entered a single JNA depot and had no real information about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that this is a single-shot rifle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, after you were appointed by the Serbian Assembly as the secretary for the secretariat of national defence, did you ever talk about that appointment - I believe you said it was in late April - with Mr. Medunjanin, who was actually serving in that position and, as you said, working in the same building with you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Either at my initiative or at Mr. Medunjanin's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You talked about the 24-hour information centre in the basement of the Municipal Assembly building. Can you tell us what kind of technical equipment was available in that facility.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That facility mostly held equipment needed for communicating information such as telephone sets, and there was also one radio station for communication with those areas that did not have telephone lines. Radio communications were developed with local communes that did not have telephone lines, and it was through that channel that we got information from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On Tuesday, you talked about, at page 18, line 7 on my LiveNote - I note that my pages were apparently different than Mr. Lukic's for some reason - that the centre is still in the same location and all the equipment and technical means that are required for work are located there. Are you saying that the only thing, technical means available, are a telephone and a radio?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that was the only thing we had. You asked me what technical equipment was located there, and I said precisely what the basic equipment of the centre was. There was also a teleprinter, a switchboard, and some other technical equipment that I really don't know much about because I'm no expert in communications, just as I'm no expert in weaponry. I didn't major in this area. I know just as much as a layman does. And I'm not denying if you have more information about this, if you tell me that there was a particular piece of equipment there that I didn't know about or didn't mention, I won't refute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. As the supervisor, as the secretary of the secretariat for several years, were you familiar, did that equipment include encryption equipment? In other words, equipment to encrypt and decipher communications?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that equipment was only connected to our organisational unit in Banja Luka. If something that was encoded came from above, we were able to decode it, to decrypt it. And our employee in charge of decoding was able to deal with such telegrams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be correct then sir that this communication centre was not for the purpose of people calling up to complain about not having electricity and water, it was for communications with higher bodies and military and police units?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would not be correct to say. It had nothing to do with police or army units because the police and the army had their own communication centres. The main purpose of our centre, however, was to collect information from the civilian sector, as I have already described. And I don't think there is any need for me to repeat it. You cannot make the link that you are trying to make because the police and the army had their own communication centres that were not linked up with our system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain, sir, why the encryption equipment was useful in collecting information from civilians and complaints about civilian life?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This equipment was not intended to collect such encrypted information. The information that was collected was collected through open telephone lines. When we got instructions from the ministry at the higher level about replenishment and reinforcement of units or about military documents that contained information such as strength of troops, et cetera, then this encrypting machine was used to decode such instructions from higher levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So among the uses of that information centre was to receive confidential, secret information about things such as army unit strength and deployments of military units. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, the centre did not do that, nor did I say that in my testimony. That part of information was gathered by the army in their own communication centres. They had information of that kind. We did not collect such information, nor was it in our purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe your answer is on the transcript. Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could the witness be shown S99.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: While that's being handed to you, sir, is it correct that among the information received in this information centre would be instructions from the republic level political leadership to municipal bodies such as the Crisis Staff and the president of the Municipal Assembly? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if that occurred in the afternoon when these institutions were not working, then it was the central telephone downstairs or the fax machine that received such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you're now being shown the document which is handed to you, S99 in this case. As you can see, it is a letter, and the person whose name appears at the bottom as a signatory is Dr. Radovan Karadzic. The title used is "President of the Serbian democratic party of Bosnia-Herzegovina" and it is addressed "to all the presidents of municipalities." Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could the document in the meantime please be placed in the ELMO in a way that we can see the entire page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Referring to the fourth paragraph, you can read along with me, is it correct that Dr. Karadzic indicates that the "municipalities now face an obligation to urgently connect their own information centres with the regional centres if it has not been done so far and provide for the personnel and other requirements to monitor the situation in the field, keeping in mind the current situation in the republic, it is necessary to cooperate with the public security service by providing the centres with a duty shift and ability to convey and receive information 24 hours a day nonstop, Saturdays and Sundays." And then the next paragraph -- excuse me two paragraphs down, the letter continues: "With regard to the above, it would be useful if you personally inform yourself about the state of affairs in the information centres in your municipality as well as their performance capabilities." Sir, do you understand this letter, from what you see in it, to be referring to the type of information centre that you had in the basement of the Municipal Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the opportunity to see this letter, and I didn't act on the orders of the president of the Serbian democratic party. But I don't see any contradiction here. I told you that we were connected to the regional centre in Banja Luka and that we performed duties within the purview of the civilian structures and we exchanged information with other end-users of that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, it's consistent with what you told us about the use of the information centre. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am required to say yes here then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just make clear: You're never required to say yes unless that's the truth. I just was asking you for an answer. Sir, you mentioned that President Stakic would come by the information centre, that Mr. Drljaca and Mr. Zeljaja would sometimes stop by. Why did they stop by the information centre, given that they had their own communications available in the police and in the army, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they would stop by in the afternoon, given the nature of the duties that were performed. They were interested in what was going on in the town. There were shortages of electricity, lack of water. Water would be poisoned. There were outbreaks of contagious diseases. And I didn't object to them coming and inquiring as to what the situation in town was like. I thought it only normal for them to be interested in that. I didn't have any other contacts with them. We didn't talk about anything else. The president of the municipality also came to inquire about the situation, and so did others, other people who were interested in the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, did Mr. Drljaca and Zeljaja and Dr. Stakic stop by your office during working hours or only stop by and meet you at that information centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped by my office very rarely. President Stakic came to my office only once, as far as I can remember. And Mr. Drljaca and Mr. Zeljaja never visited my office during the working hours. When we saw each other, it would be at the meetings in the Municipal Assembly and occasionally when one of them would stop by the early warning and information centre, the reason being that I used to spend quite a lot of time there, and that's where they could find me, and that's where they would come to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you say "the meetings at the Municipal Assembly," are you referring to the Crisis Staff meetings, the National Defence Council meetings, Municipal Assembly meetings, or all three?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on when meetings took place. First, there would be the National Defence Council meeting, and then there would be the Crisis Staff meetings. There were sessions of the Assembly, and there were other contacts and appointments regardless of the formal meetings. Some questions were being discussed, and some issues dealt at informal meetings. For example, I would meet with the secretary for economy or the president of the Municipal Assembly without actually scheduling a meeting or outside the formal meetings of any of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the meetings of the National Defence Council take place - in 1992 I'm talking about - take place in the same location as the meetings of Crisis Staff, the room near the president's office that you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You mentioned Tuesday, on page 24, line 12, that "the president of the assembly had a direct line with the chief of the SUP." Do you know what the purpose of that direct line was between Dr. Stakic and Mr. Drljaca's office?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the president had a direct line with the chief of the SUP. I said that before the arrival of both Mr. Stakic and Mr. Drljaca and myself to these offices, there were functional lines among all the officials, the president of the League of Communists, the president of the Municipal Assembly, the secretary of the secretariat for national defence. So they were the so-called functional lines, three numbers, three-digit numbers, so that they could all sort of establish a conference call if you wish. I did not use this connection. I didn't need to use it. Whether somebody else used this functional connection for some purposes, I don't know. You would have to sort of ask other people. I never used this functional line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I understand you didn't use it. I'm just going to read your testimony from Tuesday on page 24, beginning on line 10, just to make sure you feel it's accurate and do not want to correct or change it. At the end of line 10, you began: "In addition to telephone numbers, there were some functional numbers with three digits, and those were direct lines between the president of the municipality, the chief of the SUP." So that would be accurate. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but I would like to add to that that it was not just between these two persons. There was a line at the territorial staff at the secretariat for defence, in the former office of the League of Communists. And I said, and it is correct, that there was a line between the president of the Municipal Assembly and the chief of SUP, but there were also other offices connected by means of that line. Now, as to who used this line and for what purposes, I don't know. I don't agree that this line existed only between these two offices. There were seven or eight different offices and different officials connected by means of that functional line. So not only the president of the Municipal Assembly and the chief of SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] These were eight of the most important officials, people fulfilling the most important --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: These were eight of the most important officials, people fulfilling the most important functions in the municipality. Would that be correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the previous law and the previous system, and this was the legacy of that system. This is what we inherited for the former system. In some of the offices where this line existed, according to the new organisation and new distribution of power, this stopped existing. Some of the functions -- some of the positions were abolished, so these telephones still existed in the offices, but people were simply not there because some of the positions were abolished. And that's when these telephone lines were disconnected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, after the takeover of power, when you took over the position of the secretary of the secretariat, when was the next time you saw Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether it was in the period of three, five, or seven days, whether that was the time interval. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you had this first meeting with him that you recall, was it an individual meeting or was it in a meeting of a body such as the Crisis Staff, National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was not functioning at the time, so it was not at a meeting of the Crisis Staff. I can't remember whether this was the session of the National Defence Council or whether we had a sort of met just the two of us. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You were shown during your testimony minutes of the meetings of the National Defence Council on the 15th of May and the 29th of May. How many meetings of the National Defence Council do you think you attended in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it more than ten?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you attend more meetings than the two that we discussed in your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the witness be shown S28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, before we are leaving the actual document, and in order not to have to return to this document, may I ask a question based on this document. Previously your testimony was that this document would be in line with your previous testimony. We can see that this letter was dated March 23, 1992. The follow-up question would be: When was this centre in the municipality -- in the building of the Municipal Assembly established under the special circumstances? I recall very well that you mentioned that there was always such a centre in the past and afterwards. But when were these measures requested by Mr. Karadzic the 23rd of March 1992 established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what measures he asked for and what measures were taken on Mr. Karadzic's orders. I didn't have those documents, and I never acted on any of such documents. As far as I can remember, I acted on the order that arrived from a superior body in Banja Luka. And according to that order, we were supposed to introduce a 24-hour duty for the purpose of the Crisis Staff. We established that service, and it is mentioned in the document that the on-duty service is established for the purposes of the civilian sector. I didn't see this document before. I see it for the first time, so I really don't know who asked for what measures and what measures were implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You just say you don't know who asked for what measures. By whom was this letter you have before you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And who was the recipient of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stakic. I apologise. I'm not looking at the date. But it says "to all the presidents of municipalities" and it is on the 22nd March of 1992. The president of our municipality was not Dr. Stakic, but Mr. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was there a president of a shadow government at that time, Mr. Budimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know any such thing, nor did I participate in any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be realistic, do you believe that a letter of this kind would be addressed to Professor Cehajic, being not a member of the SDS, but written by the president of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally, I think that it wouldn't. But in my previous answer, I've said that I don't know that I didn't participate, that I didn't receive this letter, and that I didn't participate in the implementation of any measures relative to this letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What was that important with this letter that we can read "destroy after reading"? In the headline of this letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I didn't write this letter. I didn't consider the importance of that letter and what it contains, and I never had this letter in my hands before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, just to follow up a bit, you told us that you were not a member of the SDS in 1992 and did not join the party until 1994. Do you feel that you were within, in 1992, do you feel that within the Crisis Staff and the National Defence Council there was an inner circle who were members of the party who were more trusted than people like yourself and Mr. Travar?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm glad that you have asked me that and that you have mentioned that I became a member of the party in 1994, because I wanted to add something to what I said yesterday. When you asked me, I said "yes," bearing in mind something that reflects the truth, and that is that in my statement given to the investigators of the Prosecution, I explained the circumstances under which I became a member of the SDS. It was not my free choice. I was selected as a member of the municipal board by a higher body, and I would like to mention that, something that I've already said to the investigators. And as for your question, sir, it is my personal opinion that this would reflect the truth. Some other people enjoyed more trust than me. And as for Mr. Travar, you can ask him the same question, and I'm sure he will give you his own personal views of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, as a citizen of Prijedor, weren't you aware that in January of 1992, although you were not a member of the SDS, there was the formation of a separate Serbian municipality, a shadow government, and Dr. Stakic was made the president of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information from the media about the establishment of the Assembly of the Serbian People. This appeared on the media. I believe that it was in January. So whatever was public information, I had the same information. As for the shadow government, I don't have the exact information, and I can't tell you anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the purpose of the transcript, I don't think it's worth showing to the witness, but I would refer the Court to S96, which is a document signed by Dr. Stakic, President of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Prijedor dated 17 January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, going back to the National Defence Council, I believe the witness --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me. I am not denying that this is his signature, as you you're saying that it is. I just said what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it would be fair enough that the witness be shown this document nevertheless. We have the necessary time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, in the meantime, on page 14, line 22, you mentioned "some other people enjoyed more trust than me." Who would be these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those people were prominent members of the party who were members and officials of the municipality organs. And it appeared to me that they enjoyed more trust than me. I've told you that when I was appointed, I was not a member of the party and that it was not a final solution. They respected me, and the only thing I know is that people did not have any objections to the performance of my duties because I always respected the law. But as far as information goes, I was not so close to the source of information. I was not treated in the same way. I don't know how to put it, how to explain to you what I felt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please add names to your answer, the question who would be these people. And you referred: "Members of the parties who were members and officials of the municipal organs." Could you please give us the names you are referring to in your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said. President of the municipality, vice-president, chief of the public security station, the president of the Executive Board, these were the leading individuals in the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And in a hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said president of the municipality, vice-president, president of the Executive Board, vice-president of the Executive Board, and chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be the de jure situation. What about the de facto situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] De facto, I can't tell you anything for a fact because I don't have the proved facts and documents to corroborate that. I have explained in my testimony how people socialised, who socialised with whom. But as for your question, I cannot be precise in giving you any answer because that would be beyond the scope of what I knew, and I can't tell you something that I am not positive about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Absolutely. And it is not the duty and not the obligation for a witness to give us opinion. If a witness so wants, there is no problem with this. Of course, based on the facts, and the facts are your meetings with the acting persons in 1992 in Prijedor. Would you, for example, come to the conclusion that one of the members of the Crisis Staff played a more dominant role as the others, for example, Mr. Travar playing an exceptional role, or anybody else, in a way trying to get a stronger position than, say, Dr. Stakic or Mr. Savanovic or others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your question is very general. But if you want me to say something about Mr. Travar, I can. But I adhere to my statement, and I claim that the leaders had more influence by virtue of their positions. They were closer to the source of information; therefore, they had more influence. The only information I received was from the Ministry of Defence, and those people who were in the leading positions received more information and information is power. That gives you the right and gives you the ability to influence events and people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear answer. Please, Mr. Koumjian, sorry for having interrupted you once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I believe we were going to show the witness S96. May that be put on the ELMO, and the B/C/S handed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, this is just the document that I referred to. Do you recognise this as a document issued by the Assembly of the Serbian People of the Prijedor Municipality dated the 17th of January 1992, apparently decision number 3 of 1992. And the signatory, the person -- the name at the bottom, the title is "president of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Prijedor Municipality, Dr. Milomir Stakic." Just, sir, we wanted to give you an opportunity to look at that document and to make any comment if you wish to make any comment on this decision to join the Autonomous Region of Bosnian Krajina. If you don't have any comment, perhaps that's okay.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any comments. I have already said that I didn't take part in these processes and events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, let's now go to S28, minutes. S28, the document you've just been handed has the title "Minutes of the second session of the National Defence Council of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, held on the 5th May 1992 at 1500 hours." It indicates Dr. Milomir Stakic, president of the council, chaired the meeting. Sir, if you look at the minutes, those persons listed as members attending were Dr. Milomir Stakic, and the third name is your own, Slavko Budimir. Would this -- the document refresh your recollection that there was a meeting of the National Defence Council at least on the 5th of May, if not sooner, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that clearly. But I said yesterday, if a date is written on the paper, then I can hardly argue with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I want to go through some of the people listed as "members" of the council. In addition to Dr. Stakic, was Rade Javoric. Can you tell us what his function was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your name appears, Dr. Kuruzovic. And you can correct me if I am wrong, he was then the -- well, can you give us Dr. Kuruzovic's title. He was a Territorial Defence commander of some sort.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Dr. Kuruzovic, it's Mr. Kuruzovic. There was a duality at that time because there was a vacuum between the replacement of one commander and the appointment of another, an interregnum if you will. The transition of duties had not yet taken place, so both were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Then Dr. Milan Kovacevic, president of the Executive Board. Vladimir Arsic, from the 43rd Motorised Brigade. Simo Drljaca, chief of the SUP. Bosko Mandic, and Radmilo Zeljaja. So would I be correct, sir, if that I said that individuals with military positions among this group of members would be Mr. Javoric, Slobodan Kuruzovic, Vladimir Arsic, and Radmilo Zeljaja, approximately one half of the members of the council. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission, I would like to correct you. You are using the term "members of the council" and it doesn't say so here. It only says the session was attended. These people were not members of the council except for Mr. Kuruzovic and Mr. Javoric. There was such a function, council members in the TO staff. But the other people apart from Kuruzovic and Javoric were not members of the council. As it says here, they only attended. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, perhaps there's an issue of translation. But in the paragraph that we're referring to, in English, there appears to be two groups: The first are members of the council present, which begins with Dr. Stakic and ends with Mr. Zeljaja. And following that is a group of others in attendance, and that is the group of Simo Miskovic, Radenko Banovic, Ranko Travar, Vojo Pavicic, Mile Mutic, and Milenko Rajlic. Do you see in your language and would it be correct that the first group, including the military members, were the members of the council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not members of the council. I told you yesterday what the status of the National Defence Council was. It had not been established by the assembly. The assembly did not adopt a document naming members of the council as such. These people attended the session, but in accordance with the law that regulated these matters, they were not members of the council. And I stand by my view, they were not members of the council, nor members of the TO staff. Their presence there was occasional. Whatever anybody may have written here. I have expressed my view the way I see it and the way it was prescribed by law. If you wish, I can produce this law and tell you exactly who the members of the council were. I also made a reservation saying that the assembly in that form never set up this body and appointed these people by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, we're interested in how it actually functioned, rather than looking at the law right now. Do you have a recollection of how the National Defence Council functioned in 1992? Is your recollection pretty clear about that? Do you remember attending the meetings and what occurred?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you recall our conversation in March of last year in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do remember most of this part of our conversation, but I don't know what specifically you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll read to you from page 13, beginning on line 23. Mr. Malik asked you: "Were you ever part of the body named as the council of the municipal defence in Prijedor, council for national defence." And you answered: "The council for national defence was a body that was according to the law supposed to be formed in every municipality. And by the secretary of the secretariat for people's defence, according to that law, was the secretary of this, this Council for national defence." Now sir, what I'm really interested in is the next sentence of your answer. You said: "That as far as I can recall, this body never functioned, at least for the time while I was performing the function of a secretary of the secretariat of people's defence." In March of last year, can you explain why you were confused and stated that the National Defence Council never functioned while you were the secretary of the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've answered precisely the first part of the question, and I don't think there is any discrepancy between that and what I said a moment ago. As for the second part, in view of the fact that the assembly did not appoint this body formally and legally, I specified that this body had not really worked properly from the legal point of view because if the assembly did not legalise the operation of this body, it is irrelevant that it operated at all. I cannot argue with facts and the evidence produced before me, but that's how I approached this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, in your mind in March of 2002, when you said "as far as I can recall, this body never functioned," do you think you were confused between the National Defence Council and the Crisis Staff because they overlapped in membership, both were chaired by the same person, Milomir Stakic, and both performed more or less the same function?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why do you think I was confused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Because, sir, you said: "As far as I can recall, this body never functioned." And we know, we've now seen at least three minutes of meetings of the National Defence Council in which you were in attendance. So obviously, the body did function.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said something about the legality of this body. I told you how I view this matter, and I don't think I confused anything. I had so many interviews about this where I had to concentrate on this, and my memory has not gone completely after all. I hope you can accept that I'm not trying to hide anything or to mask the truth or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain -- in your last answer, you said you've had so many interviews about this matter. Aside from your interview in Banja Luka with Mr. Malik and myself in March, who else has interviewed you about this matter?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean that I had interviews with anyone apart from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, moving back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Apparently there's a problem with the mike.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just I think with the translation or at least the understanding of the translation. I think the witness just now said he didn't say that he had those interviews. But yet it was translated I didn't mean to say that I had those interviews. We'll have that checked out, but just so that we can note for the record that portion of it, because the witness is obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, no comments. If I would kindly ask the Prosecution to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, I'm sorry, but there's an issue about whether we correctly understood the translation of your answer. So I'll repeat the question. I'll just read it off my screen. I asked you: "Can you explain in your last answer you said you've had so many interviews about this matter. Aside from your interview in Banja Luka with Mr. Malik and myself in March, who else has interviewed you about this matter"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk to anybody about these issues except with you and Malik, and I said I discussed some general matters in my correspondence with Mr. Travar. I had no opportunity to talk to it about other people. And in the most recent times, when we had contacts, I didn't have contacts with anyone else. And when the Presiding Judge asked me "with whom I contacted in the last six months" I gave a precise answer. There was no need for me to discuss it in the past period because I was involved in a completely different kind of work. You must have misunderstood me. I discussed this only with you, and I discussed general matters with Mr. Travar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back to the minutes for a moment, in the list of persons not members who attended, we have several names that we recognise and whose functions we know, such as Mr. Miskovic. But can you explain the function of Mr. Radenko Banovic. What was his position and function at that time, 5th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radenko Banovic was the head of the service for property-related and legal affairs, and the land registry, or the registry of immoveable property. I don't know what it was called at the moment. Maybe it was the secretariat. But it was the unit in the municipality for property-related and legal affairs, and the registry of immoveable property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: At this meeting of the National Defence Council was Mile Mutic. Can you tell us in what function Mile Mutic attended the meeting of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Mutic, before and after, on two or three occasions, he was replaced as director of Kozarski Vjesnik. I don't know whether he was the director then and whether he was present. But he was present as the representative of that publishing house he worked for. Whether as an editor or a director or in some other capacity, but that's his line of work. And I think it was on those grounds that he attended. I can't specify whether he was the director of Kozarski Vjesnik at that moment. I can't be sure, but I know he worked for that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you have told us before about Mr. Rajlic, you mentioned his name. He was on the video, one of the persons you identified. Can you tell us the function of Milenko Rajlic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly, he was secretary for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would that be a body that dealt with the media and with communication, propaganda, if you will, or if you want to use the word communication, between the authorities and the public?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no particular body for that. We are talking about Mr. Rajlic. As far as I can remember, he never managed to actually set up that secretariat. And there was nothing like what we have in these systems here, somebody who is the spokesperson for the authorities. He was only appointed. And the system for the actual discharge of his duties was never developed as it was supposed. So he was present there, but his job as it should have been done was not actually done because there was no appropriate infrastructure and organisation established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, these minutes indicate this is the second session of the National Defence Council. The minutes you looked at the first day you testified, from the 15th of May, indicated they were the fourth session. Do you recall the third session of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember either the first or the third. I really can't play it all back in my head. I can see what's written in the minutes, and I can't remember really all these other sessions. I don't remember what happened, when, and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Sir, how often would you have contact with bodies above -- in your area of responsibility, bodies above the municipal level, with the republic or regional level?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have spoken about this in my earlier testimony. I said I had contacts only with the minister for defence and the secretary of the secretariat of national defence at the Banja Luka level which was my superior body. With the secretary of the secretariat, we had two-weekly or monthly contacts in this period. And as far as this period which you are talking about is concerned, perhaps I had one meeting with the minister of defence in August or maybe it was September. But I have already said that the issue was not a professional one, but it was a matter of families of disabled men and veterans, and the development of our system in that respect. I also said with other leaders on higher levels, I had no contact whatsoever on any grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let's confine ourselves to May of 1992 after you first assumed the position of secretary of the secretariat. Do you recall, did you have any in-person meetings with the person who headed that secretariat at the republic level in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you have any meetings with anyone at the regional level, face to face, in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: How often would you be in telephone contact, if at all, with the republic or regional levels in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you how often. That is such a broad question. Whatever I answer, often or not often. Whenever there was a need to clarify something, we had contacts. But I don't think the telephone contacts were very frequent. When something needed to be done, we had contacts, but the instructions we received were very clear and precise, and there was no particular need to talk on the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So would it be correct that you had much more frequent contacts with Dr. Stakic, Colonel Arsic, and Mr. Zeljaja than you had with your superiors at the republic and regional level. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, depending on the question and depending on the duties, everyone was treated equally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like the witness to repeat the answer. Because I think that it's wrongly reflected in the transcript. Whether it's affirmative or negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question, to remind you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, my question was, I'm going to read it off the screen: "Would it be correct you had much more frequent contacts with Dr. Stakic, Colonel Arsic, and Mr. Zeljaja, than you had with your superior at the republic or regional level. Correct?"

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was not correct. I said I had contacts with these people, depending on matters under discussion, and which I received in the form of orders. Depending on how these instructions and orders arrived, I treated these persons equally. I would kindly ask you one thing, because it also happened with the Prosecution and with the Defence as well, because you are trying to put something in my mouth, and you are trying to get me to say something. I am now having to focus on fending off attempts to put words in my mouth. I would appreciate it if I could be spared from that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise: The microphone did not really catch the first word of the witness's answer, so it was not clear whether it was correct or not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No problem, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it possible to move the microphones closer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, your secretariat was somewhat of a link between the civilian authorities who would support the armed forces and the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My secretariat discharged its duties in keeping with the law and the regulations. We did not provide any support to civilian authorities, and we didn't supply the army with anything either. We worked only in keeping with the regulations. I told you what the duties of our organ is. Recruitment, entry into military records, replenishment, and reinforcement of military units, and the rest, according to procedure. This is how I define the work of our organ. I don't see it as providing support to this or that party. In the light of the relationship between executive and legislative authority, we only had a role in executing mobilisation insofar as we exchanged information when the army asked us just for example, to mobilise an engineer who was a leader or head of unit in the post office system. They are asking us to send him to an army unit, and the post office refuses to let him go because they can't work Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. without him. Or another engineer from the waterworks is required to go to an army unit, and his company is also hard-put to spare him. That is how we worked in harmonising the needs of the army with the executive and legislative authorities, trying to make sure that the army units are -- have the strength needed, and the civilian aspects of life in town can go on more or less normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was part of your responsibility taking care of goods in the companies and things that had to be assigned to the army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only the replenishment of unit with men and materiel and technical supplies was under our authority. But only some supplies. The army already had heavy machinery and vehicles, so they already had 90 per cent of the equipment. And as for us, we would only replenish the army with supplies, with 10 per cent supplies that we got from the companies. We didn't supply the army with any types of goods save for the materiel and technical equipment, and the manpower. And the materiel and the technic the equipment strictly according to the prescribed regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before I give the floor to Defence counsel, I would kindly ask Prosecution counsel also to mention the page of the previous statement he is referring to. Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We are aware that this witness sometimes speaks very fast, and that the translators cannot catch every his word. But we think that it's very crucial. When he was explaining on page 29, line 10 --

utterances.text: May I once again the Prosecution counsel, before the break, to repeat this question. I think that's the easiest way to cure alleged misinterpretations of the answers of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In this instance, Your Honour, could I read the answer and ask the witness to correct the translation if there's any problem? I'll read the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that they were contacting...

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said you would read the answer for me to correct. So that's what I'm waiting for. Do you now want me to repeat my answer, or are you going to read my answer back to me and then ask me to correct whatever I think is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, the counsel of the Prosecution did that what I wanted him to do, to repeat the question, allowing you to give the correct answer. So please be so kind and answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry for confusing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again, Mr. Budimir. It's my fault. The question I asked was: "Was part of your responsibility taking care of goods in the companies and things that had to be assigned to the army?"

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was no. This was not our responsibility. We only had to replenish the units with conscripts and materiel and technical equipment. That is what I said in my answer. I apologise. Maybe I should slow down a little. I'll try to adjust my speed in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And further in compliance with His Honour's orders just before the break, sir I'm going to read to you the question I asked you in Banja Luka in March, and your answer. And if you feel it needs to be corrected in any way, please do so. I asked you beginning on line 17, page 23: "Your secretariat was somewhat of a link between those civilian authorities who would support the armed forces and the army. Is that correct?" You answered: "Okay, yes, we were, because we were actually on the borderline because we took care of the people who had to go into the army, had to go into the police, who were assigned to the civilian protection, to the work obligation, so on. And we were also taking care of the goods and the companies, you know, the things had to be assigned to the army, to the companies. And so, and so. So basically, we dealt with the distribution of both, the people into the units and the materiel goods. We had first of all you do have to understand that we had no power to issue any orders towards the army or the police or the civilian protection, or the companies or institutions. Our task was to secure conditions for them to be able to work." Do you stand by that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that we have translation, I don't see any discrepancy here. If we have understood each other well, we are talking about the place where the word "goods" was mentioned. But I was talking about the materiel and technical equipment. And in that sense, we were some sort of a link between the municipality and the army. It was our obligation to create the conditions for the companies to work, to have enough people, and for the army to have enough people. We also had to make sure that the companies had enough technical equipment to be able to work, like, for example, the water supplies and other companies. At the same time, we had to make sure that the army had enough vehicles because their needs were increased at the time. So this would be in keeping what I said previously. If you will allow me, I would like to say that we didn't keep a record on any goods that were assigned to the army. So we could not dispose with them. What our duty was, was to keep record on conscripts and materiel and technical equipment. That was our only responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We should not forget, as I did yesterday, from the Prosecution, there was tendered an enlargement of a previously admitted document. It was the article from Kozarski Vjesnik dated 12th of June 1992 with the headline "Becir Medunjanin arrested." Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence as S162/5B-1. The trial stays adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I misplaced my notes, so I'm going to be more disorganised than normal, even more disorganised. But if the witness could be given a new document. utterances.text: Sir, in 1995, were you still in your position now part of the Ministry of Defence, that is, the municipal National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to correct something that was said about my personal status. Can I be given the permit to do that now, or maybe towards the end of my testimony? If I am given the permit to do it now, I would like to answer the question after that.

utterances.text: Mr. Budimir, this is your testimony. And whenever you want to correct or amend something, you may do so. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yesterday, the Defence and the Prosecution asked me detailed questions on my marital status and my family status. I would like to say that one of the Prosecution witnesses in this trial is (redacted) He said something untruthful. He actually said a lie about my father. He stated that my father was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed one word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that my father participated in the people's defence war from 10th of February 1994 to 1945 [as interpreted]. utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, would please the transmission be stopped and redacting on the delay the name that the witness mentioned as soon as possible. And I think Your Honour understands the reason.

utterances.text: Yes. Of course, but the name is not reflected on the transcript. We can resolve the problem --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, as soon as possible. Please, Madam Registrar, it's urgent. May I ask you, please, to write down the name of the person you just mentioned. Additionally, I have to ask you ex officio, how did you learn about this information on another witness appearing here -- let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, has the document been given to the witness, the conclusions of the 14th session of the war presidency. And could the English be put on the ELMO please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is already on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, in 1995, did you still hold the position of secretary of the municipal secretariat for national defence? And you can correct the title if I've misstated it at that time.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was still heading that organ, but this organ had the status of a section in the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. It was not a municipal organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. In this document, you are mentioned as having attended this particular meeting on the last page -- excuse me, you're mentioned on the last page as -- in point number 2 of agenda item number 3. There's a direction to you. First, can you tell us, this war presidency in August of 1995, can you explain what it was.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war presidency was a body which was also appointed according to the instructions from higher authorities. I don't know now who exactly gave this order. I think it must have been the president of the state or the government that gave the order in the Official Gazette to form war presidencies at Municipal Assembly level, or maybe it was the assembly of Republika Srpska. I don't know. The instruction for the establishment of this war presidency was received by the person who was then acting as president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Who were the members of the war presidency of Prijedor Municipality in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember who occupied which post and who was named member of the presidency by appointment. I believe there was a decision on the appointment of these people from a higher authority, but I can't remember now who these people were, who were the members, and how many there were. If you refresh my memory, perhaps I could help you. I can't enumerate all these members. I think there was a president of the Executive Board. I believe there was a conflict whether this post would be occupied by the president of the assembly or a deputy to the assembly. I don't know who the other members were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps this document may refresh your recollection. Looking at agenda item number 1, point number 4, it states that "The war presidency members, Veljko Djukic, Vlado Vujcic, and Dr. Milomir Stakic visit the garrison after 2200 hours and gather information about the military situation." Were these three individuals named the three members of the war presidency of Prijedor in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Mr. Djukic, I am certain. About Mr. Vlado Vujcic, I don't know and I don't know about Mr. Stakic either. I don't know which posts they occupied. It is possible that the decision appointed them members. Ex officio, they were not supposed to be unless there was a special decision on their appointment to the War Presidency. It is possible that they were members too but I can only tell you for sure about Mr. Djukic because he was president of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If you look at agenda item number 3, this is a rough translation that we have, so I would ask you to read the first point on agenda item number 3. To be sure that we have the correct translation, can you read that slowly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By 1700 hours, one group of the working war presidency --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. On agenda item number 3 on the last page, if you could read the first -- point number 1. It's at the end of the document. There are three points. And the paragraph just above the one that contains your name. I mean point number 1. I'm looking at the English only. But agenda item number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So the transcript is clear, this is page number 02140 -- sorry, I have to restart. 02147071. And we discuss the bottom part of this document, the three last paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first item reads: "The Presidency hereby adopts the conclusion that Momcilo Radanovic, vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, be acting president of the Municipal Assembly until the election of the president."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, would it be correct that Mr. Radanovic became acting president until Milomir Stakic was then again elected the president of Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I cannot place this in time, the moment when Mr. Radanovic, or rather Mr. Stakic resumed his function as president, I believe that after Mr. Radanovic, Mr. Maric became president. Mr. Stakic was before this gentleman. I really have to say that I'm not sure about this. But I was president of the Executive Board in 1996/1997, and I think Radanovic occupied this post before Maric. The changes were frequent. All I know is that for a while, Mr. Kurnoga was in this post, and he was replaced, and there were problems with this war presidency, whether the president of the Municipal Assembly would head this war presidency or it would be a deputy to the assembly. You will have to excuse me, really, on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you were vice-president of the Executive Board in 1996 and 1997, was Dr. Stakic again the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stakic was on this post then. But I was vice-president of the Executive Board when Mr. Stakic was president. Whether Mr. Radanovic was vice-president while Mr. Stakic was president -- anyway, Mr. Stakic was on this post for a while. And then came Maric, and during Maric's term of office, my term of office expired after the multiparty elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm trying to place this in time. Did Dr. Stakic become again the president of the municipality to the best of your recollection before the end of war, before December 1995, or after the end of the war, after the signing of the Dayton accords?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot place this in time now, but I don't think it's any problem to establish that. There must be a decision of the assembly on this. I know when President Stakic was replaced in 1992/1993, he became president of the assembly, and he was president of the assembly while I was vice-president of the Executive Board. When he was appointed by the relevant decision exactly, I don't know. I know my decision was received in June or July and was valid for eight months. I think this fact can be established very clearly independently of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. At this time, the body you headed was the branch of a republic level body, the department of defence or Ministry of Defence. And yet, in point number 2 on agenda item 3, the next paragraph to what you just read the war presidency apparently has issued a conclusion that Slavko Budimir assign an expert from the defence ministry department who shall, in cooperation with an officer in charge of defence issues of the municipal bodies, prepare a draft on war systemisation of the municipal administrative bodies. So, sir, even in 1995, did municipal bodies continue to give directions to the body you headed which was then part of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. We would object because this is irrelevant and outside the scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is, no doubt, in line with the questions put to this witness, and all the previous witnesses, and no doubt, the acts as such are not in the framework -- in the timely framework of the indictment, but it has to do something with the role and the character of Dr. Stakic. And therefore, dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, were you able to follow my rather convoluted question, or would you like me to restate it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I followed the question. The decision that came from a higher level appointed me member of that war presidency, and I was acting chief of section, that section being a state body. If I can ask you to go back to the earlier appointment of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Simo Drljaca was also appointed to that Crisis Staff, which was a republican organ. And in this case, it is not an order issued to a municipal body by a republican body. It is only a case of this body being requested to provide something. The municipal body could always ask from a republican body, to make certain reports, drafts, documentation, et cetera. In this case, nobody issued me with an order to do something, nor did this order have a basis in the law saying that pursuant to the law, this and that, article so and so. Our body was asked to help with the preparation of wartime systemisation, because we were the most professional in this area. We knew the number of enterprises, companies, their staffs, et cetera, and we could determine how many people could be allocated. And I believe it is in this sense, along this line, that this request was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: From the time you joined the SDS party in 1994 through the summer of 1997, did Dr. Stakic remain politically active in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time when I was a member of the SDS, from 1993, or rather 1994 onwards, I believe Mr. Stakic, or rather Dr. Stakic, was active as long as he was president of the Municipal Assembly. But when he left that post, he stopped taking active part in the work of the party and in the work of these bodies. While he was president, it was normal for him to take part in the work of the municipal board of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If you know, did Dr. Stakic, after leaving the municipal office, the office of president of the assembly, continue to attend party meetings and be a prominent member of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think so. I don't feel he did. I cannot even tell you exactly when he left his post and whether he continued to be in the party and to be a prominent member for a while longer. I believe he was an active member as long as he held the post that he held. After that, I don't know how actively he worked in the party and for how long. I can't tell you precisely yes or no. I can only say as much as I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know on the document you saw before you, where Dr. Stakic's named as a member of the war presidency, when he became a member of the war presidency and who appointed him to that position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it existed, and I don't want to say it did, I think many more people were appointed to the war presidency than to the Crisis Staff. So if he was a appointed to that presidency, he was appointed by some higher organ, maybe the presidency, maybe the assembly. Anyway, somebody from upstairs. Some people were appointed by name to this war presidency, because I know that I was appointed to that war presidency myself. And I believe Mr. Djukic was named as president of the Executive Board, or maybe as a deputy of the assembly. He received that enactment which said that certain people were appointed to the war presidency. All I know is that there were more members of the presidency than there were members of the Crisis Staff. And they were named not only by the function, by the posts they held. There were also other people who didn't occupy specific posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, because the transcript is not quite clear on this issue. On page 43, line 24, Mr. Budimir, you stated: "If I can ask you to go back to the earlier appointment of the Crisis Staff, Mr." and then until now it wasn't possible to catch up the name, "was also appointed to that Crisis Staff which was a republican..." and then the word is missing. Could you please repeat this part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that Mr. Drljaca was appointed to the municipal Crisis Staff. He was chief of the public security station. And that was a body at the republican level. At the republican level, there was the Ministry of the Interior and the public security station was an organisational unit of the ministry, just the same way I was vice-president of the Executive Board, and Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter lost this part. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please repeat. The interpreter has lost the last part of the answer. It reads: "Just the same way I was vice-president of the Executive Board, and Mr. ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not what I said. I said unlike him, I was member of the Executive Board as secretary of the municipal secretariat for national defence, ex officio. But Mr. Drljaca was not a member of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly because he was chief of the public security station. And that was a state body, a single unified state body of the Ministry of the Interior. And from that state body, he could not be a member of the municipal body. I could be a member of the Executive Board, however because at that moment I was secretary of the municipal secretariat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, but nevertheless, you said in the beginning of your answer, page 46, line 3: "I said that Mr. Drljaca was appointed to the municipal Crisis Staff." So there was no problem to be on the one level, and then appointed at the same time to the municipal Crisis Staff, or did I misunderstand you? Once again, you said: "I said Mr. Drljaca was appointed to the municipal Crisis Staff. He was chief of the public security station, and that was a body of the republican level." This was your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct. But I also said earlier that by a decision, whether it was the president or the presidency, the Crisis Staff was appointed naming by name the people occupying certain posts who would be members of that staff. And they were consulted in that context on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Mr. Koumjian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you said yesterday, on page 49 of the LiveNote, beginning on line 11, you were talking about the relationship between the Crisis Staff and army or police. And you said: "But as far as pointing out of problems in the territory of the municipality, and the taking of measures to prevent repetition of such incidents, it was the obligation of municipal bodies to point out such things and to ask the competent authorities to take whatever measures were necessary to redress any deficiencies and problems." Sir, in any of the meetings that you attended, did Dr. Stakic ever complain of crimes committed by the army or police against the non-Serbian population of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you that we did have situations of that kind and discussions. And when things culminated with the events in Prijedor that went outside of the law and the measures prescribed by the law, certain Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. authorities did not take appropriate measures. Dr. Stakic asked the public security station to restore law and order in town, and also he asked the army to keep their military conscripts under control. Throughout the time, even when certain members of the army were on leave, they still belonged to the army, and they should be under the control of the army. Everybody in the presidency, including Dr. Stakic, asked for these illegal acts on the territory of Prijedor to be put an end to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Specifically, what illegal acts are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about plunder, killings, disorder, arson, and other similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are you talking about crimes specifically directed against Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the acts which were targeted at everybody across the board, although one could say objectively that they were mostly targeted at Muslims, and maybe Croats to a lesser extent, as well as Serbs to a lesser extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness specified that they were discussing the crimes in the city. And it's not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Budimir? You were discussing crimes in the city of Prijedor rather than the outlying areas of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The jurisdiction of the president of the municipality and municipal organs is the entire territory, so what I had in mind is the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you discuss, then, the detention of thousands of Muslims and Croats at the Keraterm and Omarska camps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated - I believe it was yesterday - that the subject matter relative to these collection centres was not on the agenda of the meetings of the Crisis Staff, and that I don't have any information on that. Or that I did not attend any of the sessions of the Crisis Staff where these matters would be discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, did you discuss specifically the massacre in July of 1992 at the Keraterm facility in the Crisis Staff where people in town heard shooting for hours at night from automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent nights outside the town. My house is about 6 kilometres from the city centre. And I was not in the position to hear that. Subsequently, I learned about the events, but I don't have any precise information as to what had happened. Nobody reported on that to anybody, and we did not receive any reports at the Crisis Staff. We didn't discuss those events at the sessions that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the massacre at Koricanska Stijena of over 200 men on a convoy escorted by Prijedor police having left Tukovi and Trnopolje headed towards Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, I never discussed that with anybody, within the purview of my organ, this was not under my jurisdiction and under my authority. This was under the jurisdictions of the Ministry of the Interior. I don't know what happened there. I was not in the position to be informed about that at any formal sessions. Nobody ever reported on that event at any of the formal sessions of any of the formal organs or bodies that I was a member of, and I did not receive any official information on what happened at that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: At any of the meetings that you attended, did Dr. Stakic complain or criticise the army for its actions in Hambarine in May, 23rd of May; in Kozarac, between the 24th and 26th of May; and in the cleansing of the Brdo region in July?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO BUDIMIR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not discuss that at the Crisis Staff, and I don't know about him criticising that. I don't know whether he said anything about that in his public appearances. In any case, this was not the subject matter of our discussions, and I never heard of the president criticising that at any official meetings.
